sample_unit: patient information materials (annexures: PILs and ChatGPT-generated equivalents)

links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-generated patient education materials versus traditional leaflets (FRE, GFI, FKGL)
links.effect: PILs more readable than ChatGPT: FRE 62.25 vs 48, GFI 11.85 vs 13.65, FKGL 8.33 vs 10.23 (P<0.05); ChatGPT text at higher grade level.
links.quote: Traditional PILs generally exhibited higher readability (P values < 0.05), with [mean (standard deviation)] FRE [62.25 (1.6) versus 48 (3.7)], GFI [11.85 (0.9) versus 13.65 (0.7)], and FKGL [8.33 (0.5) versus 10.23 (0.5)] but varied emotional tones, often negative, compared to more positive sentiments in ChatGPT-generated texts.

links.outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated patient materials
links.effect: ChatGPT materials had FKGL 10.23 vs 8.33 for PILs and lower Flesch Reading Ease (48 vs 62.25), i.e., harder to read.
links.quote: Traditional PILs generally exhibited higher readability (P values < 0.05), with [mean (standard deviation)] FRE [62.25 (1.6) versus 48 (3.7)], GFI [11.85 (0.9) versus 13.65 (0.7)], and FKGL [8.33 (0.5) versus 10.23 (0.5)] but varied emotional tones, often negative, compared to more positive sentiments in ChatGPT-generated texts.

screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT-generated patient education materials against traditional patient information leaflets for chronic pain medications using expert review and readability metrics, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
